output.proposal: By its title, HB No. 11216 seeks to create an Independent People's Commission to investigate anomalies in all government infrastructure projects; however, the text available for review is a higher education measure, the proposed "Higher Education Development and Innovation Act of 2025," which continues the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), restates its powers and funds, and repeals RA No. 7722. The title-text discrepancy should be resolved before the substantive review proceeds.
output.alignment: Under Government Organization and Mandates, the review should first establish which text is the measure actually filed, since the title proposes a new investigative commission on infrastructure anomalies while the available text reorganizes CHED. If the title governs, the review should examine how the proposed commission would fit with existing bodies, including the Independent Commission for Infrastructure created under EO No. 94 (2025), and whether it adds an overlapping investigative mandate contrary to the streamlining intent of the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). If the text governs, the review should examine whether the restated CHED mandate, including Section 4 (Commission on Higher Education) and Section 13 (Quasi-Judicial Powers of the Commission), duplicates or reallocates functions held by TESDA and other bodies. The Infrastructure Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework is relevant only to the measure as titled; the available text does not relate to infrastructure. No LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item was identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11216, as titled, seeks to create an Independent People's Commission to investigate anomalies in government infrastructure projects; the available text, however, seeks to continue and restructure the Commission on Higher Education. Its salient features, as stated in the text, are as follows:
a. Section 1 (Short Title) provides that the Act shall be known as the Higher Education Development and Innovation Act of 2025.
b. Section 4 (Commission on Higher Education) provides that CHED, created under RA No. 7722, continues as an independent body attached to the Office of the President for administrative purposes, covering public and private HEIs, while TESDA retains authority over associate degree, diploma and non-degree programs and National Universities keep their legislated autonomy.
c. Section 5 (Composition of the Commission) provides that the Commission is composed of five full-time members, a Chairperson and four Commissioners appointed by the President, who must hold earned doctorates, have at least ten years in higher education and not have been candidates in the immediately preceding election.
d. Section 7 (Rank and Emoluments) provides that the Chairperson shall have the rank and emoluments of a Department Secretary and the Commissioners the equivalent rank of an Undersecretary.
e. Section 9 (Powers and Functions of the Commission) provides developmental powers, among them formulating higher education plans, coordinating with DepEd, TESDA and the PRC, and broadening access for disadvantaged students.
f. Section 10 (Secretariat and the Executive Director) provides that a Secretariat headed by an Executive Director, assisted by two Deputy Executive Directors, shall be organized, with the Commission fixing its staffing pattern and compensation scheme.
g. Section 13 (Quasi-Judicial Powers of the Commission) provides that the Commission shall have exclusive original jurisdiction over the opening, closure and maintenance of HEIs, including SUCs and LUCs, with rules to be published within sixty days of effectivity.
h. Section 14 (Higher Education Development Fund) provides that the Fund continues to receive shares of travel tax, professional registration fee and PCSO lotto collections, may receive contributions from government financing institutions, and may have a private portion from tax-exempt donations.
i. Section 25 (Appropriations) provides that initial implementation shall be charged to CHED's current-year appropriations and thereafter included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
j. Section 27 (Repealing Clause) provides for the repeal of RA No. 7722 and of inconsistent laws and issuances.
output.related_measures_policy: As titled, HB No. 11216 may be considered alongside SB No. 1215, which bears the same title, and alongside EO No. 94 (2025) creating the Independent Commission for Infrastructure; on that reading, the measure relates to the Infrastructure Development priority of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, and the review should assess whether a new investigative commission would duplicate existing bodies, consistent with the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). As written, however, the text concerns higher education and should be read against RA No. 7722, which Section 27 (Repealing Clause) repeals, RA No. 7796 as referenced in Section 4 (Commission on Higher Education), and RA No. 9593 as referenced in Section 14 (Higher Education Development Fund). The review should first confirm the correct text of the bill with the House of Representatives before assessing its fiscal and organizational implications.

fiscal_requirements.detail: Charged to the current year's appropriations of CHED; no amount stated

Higher Education Development Fund receives 40% of travel tax collections, 30% of Professional Registration Fee collections and 1% of PCSO lotto gross sales
Government financing institutions may contribute 3% to 5% of their unimpaired surplus of the preceding year
Donations to the Fund are exempt from donor's tax and deductible for income tax purposes
Chairperson with the rank of Department Secretary and four Commissioners with the rank of Undersecretary, all full-time
Secretariat headed by an Executive Director with two Deputy Executive Directors; staffing pattern and compensation scheme fixed by the Commission
